description: We are three students from Peshawar, Pakistan, participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge as Echoes Beyond Earth. We aim to explore NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars through creative research, technology, and storytelling, highlighting its scientific and historical importance.
summary: Echoes Beyond the Earth is an interactive website that tells the stories of NASA’s discarded machines on the Moon and Mars, for the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge. Students, teens and the public can explore seven machines: the Apollo Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity and the Dawn spacecraft. Each has a sourced seven-part story, with real photos and rotatable 3D models from NASA 3D Resources. A 3D Moon and Mars mission map shows where the machines were left. A timeline, quiz with leaderboard and collectible badges make learning playful. These machines went silent, but their discoveries still echo through the science and inspiration they left behind. Our site makes sure their stories are heard, so abandoned does not mean forgotten.
details:
What it does: a single-page web app where users explore seven NASA machines left behind on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. Each machine has a seven-part story (why it was sent, its journey, what it did, what happened afterward, its legacy, a timeline and sources), real NASA photos and a rotatable 3D view.
Benefits and impact: it turns forgotten missions into something students and the public enjoy and remember, through a 3D mission map, timeline, quiz with leaderboard and badges.
Tools: JavaScript, React, Vite, Three.js (React Three Fiber and drei), Framer Motion, Node.js, Express, optional MongoDB, deployed on Vercel. Tested with Playwright.
Creativity: real NASA 3D models of the Apollo Lunar Module, Mars rovers and Ingenuity, plus a 3D Moon and Mars map with markers at the landing sites.
Limits: map marker positions are approximate. The Lunar Rover, Sojourner and Dawn use our own stylized, clearly labelled 3D illustrations, since no official models were used.
